ResetCommands.Comment: Also swapped these two lines so he will wear something.

Rooms.Name: A stone bridge
Rooms.Description:
You come to a large stone bridge that span over the Midgaard river.
The road is very well built and goes in a straight line due east-west.
You can climb down to the river at the side of the bridge.

Exits.Description: The King's Road continues in a straight line to the east.
You see a path disappearing into thick forest.

Rooms.Name: The King's Road
Rooms.Description:
You stand on the King's Road, which leads east and west. The skill of
the builders is apparent, since it is impossible to notice any turn or
irregularity in the road.

Exits.Description: You see a Castle in the far east.
The King's Road continues in a straight line to the west.

Rooms.Name: On the King's Road outside the Castle
Rooms.Description:
You are standing on the King's Road. Before you is a large Castle,
evidently built not so much for strength as for beauty. It is not
totally without defenses, though, for it is surrounded by a deep moat,
and its windows are just narrow slits for archers to shoot through. To
the north there is a drawbridge across the moat.

Exits.Description: You see the drawbridge.
The King's Road continues in a straight line to the west.

Rooms.Name: On the Drawbridge
Rooms.Description:
You have arrived at the drawbridge leading into the Castle. Before
you is a huge, double-doored gate. It seems very strong. You see some
whirls in the moat.

Exits.Description:
The gate has huge, but intricately carved hinges. As the Castle itself,
it seems designed not only for strength, but also for beauty.
You see the King's Road.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You can't see much, but it seems that something beneath the surface
is creating them.

Rooms.Name: The Kitchen
Rooms.Description:
You are in the Kitchen. Lots of helpers hurry to do the Chief Cook's
bidding, and there is a wonderful smell that makes you feel very hungry.
All around the room, there are shelves with different kinds of cooking
gear stacked on them. There is an exit to the north, and one to the
east; both leading to small passages.

Exits.Description: You see a small, dimly lit passage.
You see a small, dimly lit passage.

Rooms.Name: A small passage
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a small passage, that is clearly intended mostly
for the servants of the Castle. It is only dimly lit and quite narrow.
The passage leads west, and to the east there is a small door.

Exits.Description: The door is small and uninteresting.
You hear clanging of pots, and smell cooking meat.

Rooms.Name: The Entrance Hall
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the impressive Entrance Hall of the Castle. To
the north is an exit into the Great Hall. There is also an exit east, 
and a small door to the west.

Exits.Description: You see the King's Great Hall.
There seems to be a small guard room to the east.
To the south, there is a gate, that leads to the Drawbridge.
The door is small and uninteresting.

Rooms.Name: The Guard Room
Rooms.Description:
You are in a small room, evidently meant for guards currently not on
duty.  There is only one exit, back to the entrance hall.

Exits.Description: You see the Castle Entrance.

Rooms.Name: Under the Tower
Rooms.Description:
You are below one the three mighty towers of the Castle.  There are
no guards here, and you sense that this part of the Castle is largely
unused.  There are stairs going up to the tower, and there is also an
exit to the north.

Exits.Description: You see a small, dimly lit passage.
The stairs are old, but in good repair. They lead up into the tower.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The stairs are old, but in good repair. They lead up into the tower.

Rooms.Name: The Small Passage
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a small passage, that is clearly intended mainly
for the
servants of the Castle. The passage leads north and south.

Exits.Description: You see a small, dimly lit passage.
You hear the clanging of pots, and smell cooking meat.

Rooms.Name: The Great Hall
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the south-west end of the Great Hall. It is truly
vast; the roof is so high above your head, that it seems no closer than
the clouds outside. The roof is beautifully painted, by someone who must
have been a true master. The hall is very large, and could easily seat
several hundred people at a banquet.

Exits.Description: You see the King's Great Hall.
You see the King's Great Hall.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The paintings on the roof depict the great heroes and gods. One of 
the gods is fairly heavy-bellied and incredibly hairy, with a massive
beard.
Also among them are the great enemies and wrongdoers, such as the evil
Goddess Yochlol and the powerful evil Wizard Tharoecon.

Rooms.Name: The Great Hall
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the southern end of the Great Hall. It is truly
vast; the roof is so high above your head, that it seems no closer than
the clouds outside. The roof is beautifully painted, by someone who must
have been a true master. The hall is very large, and could easily seat
several hundred people at a banquet. To your north, you see King
Welmar's great throne, and to the south is the Castle Entrance.

Exits.Description: You see the part of the Great Hall where the throne is.
You see the King's Great Hall.
You see the Castle Entrance.
You see the King's Great Hall.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The paintings on the roof depict the great heroes and gods. One of 
the gods is fairly heavy-bellied and incredibly hairy, with a massive
beard.  Also among them are the great enemies and wrongdoers, such as
the evil Goddess Yochlol and the powerful evil Wizard Tharoecon.

Rooms.Name: The Great Hall
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the south-east end of the Great Hall. It is truly
vast; the roof is so high above your head, that it seems no closer than
the clouds outside. The roof is beautifully painted, by someone who must
have been a true master. The hall is very large, and could easily seat
several hundred people at a banquet.

Exits.Description: You see the King's Great Hall.
You see the King's Great Hall.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The paintings on the roof depict the great heroes and gods. One of
the gods is fairly heavy-bellied and incredibly hairy, with a massive
beard. Also among them are the great enemies and wrongdoers, such as the
evil Goddess Yochlol and the powerful, evil Wizard Tharoecon.

Rooms.Name: A passage
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a passage, that leads north and south. To the
south it leads towards one of towers.

Exits.Description: You see the small passage continue.

Rooms.Name: The passage
Rooms.Description:
You are in a passage, that leads north and south. To the east there
is an exit to the Great Hall.

Exits.Description: You see the passage continue.
You see the King's Great Hall.
You see the passage continue.

Rooms.Name: The Great Hall
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the north-west end of the Great Hall. It is truly
vast; the roof is so high above your head, that it seems no closer than
the clouds outside. The roof is beautifully painted, by someone who must
have been a true master. The hall is very large, and could easily seat
several hundred people at a banquet. To your east, you see King Welmar's
great throne, and to the west there is an exit to a passage.

Exits.Description: You see the part of the Great Hall where the throne is.
You see the King's Great Hall.
You see a passage.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The paintings on the roof depict the great heroes and gods. One of 
the gods is fairly heavy-bellied and incredibly hairy, with a massive
beard.
Also among them are the great enemies and wrongdoers, such as the evil
Goddess Yochlol and the powerful evil Wizard Tharoecon.

Rooms.Name: By the Throne in the Great Hall
Rooms.Description:
You are standing by the King's huge ivory throne. The throne is, to
an even greater degree than the Hall itself, a masterpiece. It is
intricately and beautifully carved, and it seems to be made out of a
single block of ivory, though you shiver at the thought of meeting the
animal that died to yield a piece of that size. The Hall continues to
the east, west and south.

Exits.Description: You see the King's Great Hall.
You see the King's Great Hall.
You see the King's Great Hall.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The paintings on the roof depict the great heroes and gods. One of 
the gods is fairly heavy-bellied and incredibly hairy, with a massive
beard.  Also among them are the great enemies and wrongdoers, such as
the evil Goddess Yochlol and the powerful evil Wizard Tharoecon.

It is large and very beautiful. The carvings are mainly of animals and
magic beasts.

Rooms.Name: The Great Hall
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the north-east end of the Great Hall. It is truly
vast; the roof is so high above your head, that it seems no closer than
the clouds outside. The roof is beautifully painted, by someone who must
have been a true master. The hall is very large, and could easily seat
several hundred people at a banquet. To your west, you see King Welmar's
great throne, and to the east there is an exit to a small passage.

Exits.Description: You see the part of the Great Hall where the throne is.
You see the King's Great Hall.
You see a passage.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The paintings on the roof depict the great heroes and gods. One of 
the gods is fairly heavy-bellied and incredibly hairy, with a massive
beard.  Also among them are the great enemies and wrongdoers, such as
the evil Goddess Yochlol and the powerful evil Wizard Tharoecon.

Rooms.Name: The small passage
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a small passage, that leads north and south. To
the west, there is an exit into the Great Hall.

Exits.Description: The passage continues to the north.
The passage continues to the south.
To the west you see the Great Hall.

Rooms.Name: The passage
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a north-south leading passage. There is a door to
the
east.

Exits.Description: The passage leads to a staircase.
The door is quite small and unobtrusive.
The passage continues to the south.

Rooms.Name: The servants' corridor
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a corridor, that stretches further to the east.
There are doors to the north and west. The corridor itself is mainly
used by servants, and lacks some of the beauty of the rest of the
castle.

Exits.Description: There is door there!!!
The corridor seems to come to its end a bit further east.
The door is made out of wood.

Rooms.Name: The end of the servants' corridor
Rooms.Description:
The corridor leads only west from here, but there is a door to the
north.

Exits.Description: The door leads to a room intended for the butler.
You see the corridor continue.

Rooms.Name: The Training Room
Rooms.Description:
This is the Training Room of the men of the Castle guard. It is very
large, with weapons standing in racks by all the walls. Most of the
weapons seem to be intended for training only, with blunt edges and the
like, but there are some that might be useful for real fighting. There
is a door to the north.

Exits.Description: The door is large and heavy.
You see a small passage.

Rooms.Name: The small passage
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a small passage leading north and south. There is
also an exit to the west, from which grunts, cheers and heavy blows can
be heard.

Exits.Description: The passage leads north to some stairs.
You see the passage continuing.
You see the Training Room.

Rooms.Name: The Stair Room
Rooms.Description:
You are standing below a great staircase, that leads up to the second
floor of the Castle. The stairs are made of marble, and there are
pillars carved in the likenesses of trees with little animals running up
and down the trunks.

Exits.Description: You see the passage.
The stairs lead up to the second floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Made out of marble, and as all the rest of the Castle made primarily
for beauty and with great skill.
Very nice. Squirrels and little birds all over.

Rooms.Name: The servants' quarters
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a large room, that seems to house many of the
servants.  The room is full of comfortable-looking beds. There is also a
large chest, probably containing some of the servants' belongings.

Exits.Description: The door is made out of wood.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The beds all look comfortable, despite the fact that this is just
the servants' place.

Rooms.Name: The butler's quarters
Rooms.Description:
You see at once that this must be the butler's room, for it lies in
the servants' wing, and still it is large and comfortable; almost
luxurious, in fact. There is a large bed and a drawer in the room. The
only exit is via the door to the south.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Looks very comfortable indeed.

Rooms.Name: The Guards' Barracks
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a very large room with bunks all over. It is
obvious, that this is where the guards off duty spend most of their
time, drinking and gambling or, probably, mostly sleeping.

Exits.Description: The door is large and heavy.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: They look a bit hard, but you could sleep in them.

Rooms.Name: The stairs
Rooms.Description:
You are standing by a staircase leading down. As you look down, you
notice that for the first time since you entered the castle, things are
not aesthetically made. Instead it looks more functional and
prison-like.

Exits.Description: You see the small passage.
The stairs go down to a well lit room.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
They seem to be made of granite, and stretch down into a more dimly
lit area than where you come from.

Rooms.Name: At a bend in the corridor
Rooms.Description: You are standing where the corridor bends from east to north.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the corridor continue.

Rooms.Name: The corridor
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads east and west.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the corridor continue.

Rooms.Name: The corridor
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads east and west.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the corridor continue.

Rooms.Name: The corridor
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. The corridor continues west, and to
the north you see the luxurious guest wing.

Exits.Description: You see the guest wing.
You see the corridor continue.

Rooms.Name: In the south-east tower
Rooms.Description:
This part of the tower is fairly uninteresting, but it leads further
upwards...

Exits.Description: The room at the top of the tower seems darkish for some reason.
You see the stairs at the bottom of the tower.

Rooms.Name: The corridor
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads north and south. There is
also an exit to the east here.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see a small room.
You see the corridor continue.

Rooms.Name: By the treasure room
Rooms.Description:
You are standing by a great iron door. The door is very large, and
seems very solid indeed. There is a sign posted by it.

Exits.Description: You see a large steel door.
You see the corridor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
TREASURE ROOM

   Authorized personnel only - all others keep out.
   ANY trespassing will be SEVERELY punished!!

Rooms.Name: The Great Treasury
Rooms.Description:
As you enter this room, you are astonished by the riches that are
stowed away here; not so much in gold, but paintings, tapestries,
skillful carvings and sculptures all over the vast room. You realize,
however, that most of these things are too well known to be sold
anywhere, without branding yourself as a thief, and condemning yourself
to instant death at the hands of the Royal Guard.

Exits.Description: You see a large steel door.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It seems they are stored here temporarily to enable changing of the
decoration in the Castle on a regular basis.

Rooms.Name: The Guest Wing
Rooms.Description:
You have arrived at the part of the Castle where prominent guests are
housed. To the east there is a large, ornamented door, and a somewhat
smaller one leads north.

Exits.Description: The door seems to lead to a guest room.
You see the guest suite behind the door.
You see the corridor.

Rooms.Name: The Guest Suite
Rooms.Description:
This must be where only the most highly regarded guests stay, since
it is luxurious beyond your wildest imagination. This is only the living
room  of the suite, but it is huge and tastefully decorated. All the
furniture is not only beautiful, but also made for comfort. To the
north, there is an exit to the bedroom, and there is a door to the west.

Exits.Description: You see the bedroom.
Behind the door you see the entrance to the Guest Wing.

Rooms.Name: The corridor
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads north and south.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the corridor continue.

Rooms.Name: The Ball Room
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the great Ball Room. It is a truly large room,
with a stage for an orchestra in the south-east end.

Exits.Description: You see the Ball Room.
To the east you see the stage.

Rooms.Name: By the stage
Rooms.Description:
Before you, you see the stage. It is large enough for some 40
musicians to play on at the same time. The Ball Room continues to the
west and north.

Exits.Description: You see the Ball Room.
You see the Ball Room.

Rooms.Name: A Guest Room
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a large room. Although it is comfortable enough,
you can tell it is not meant for any of the most illustrious guests,
since it lacks that extreme luxury found elsewhere in the Castle.

Exits.Description: Behind the door, you see the entrance to the Guest Wing.

Rooms.Name: The Bedroom
Rooms.Description:
This room is dominated by the huge four-poster bed, that stands
against the northern wall. The room is large and cozy, and the bed
virtually begs you to lie down in it and sleep.

Exits.Description: You see the living room of the suite.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Large, comfortable, bolstered... Invites you to sleep in it.

Rooms.Name: The corridor
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in a long corridor, decorated with tapestries
depicting old times and old heroes. It leads north and south. There is
an exit to the east, that leads to a large room.

Exits.Description: You see the corridor continue.
You see the Ball Room.
You see the corridor continue.

Rooms.Name: The Ball Room
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the great Ball Room. It is a truly large room,
with a stage for an orchestra in the south-east end.

Exits.Description: You see the Ball Room.
You see the Ball Room.
You see the corridor.

Rooms.Name: The Ball Room
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the great Ball Room. It is a truly large room,
with a stage for an orchestra in the south-east end.

Exits.Description: To the east, you can enter a tower.
To the south you see the stage.
You see the Ball Room.

Rooms.Name: In the Tower
Rooms.Description:
You are standing in the north-eastern of the three great watch-
towers of the Castle. To the west, you can enter the Ball Room and there
are stairs leading up into the Tower.

Exits.Description: You see the Ball Room.
The stairs lead a long way up to the top of the Tower.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The stairs are made out of granite, and seem solid enough.

Rooms.Name: The Grand Staircase
Rooms.Description:
You are standing on a great staircase, that leads up and down. To the
east, there is a large oak door, and a corridor leads south.

Exits.Description: The door is large and made out of oak.
You see the corridor.
The stairs continue up to the top of the tower.
The stairs lead down to the first floor of the Castle.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The stairs are made of marble, and there are pillars carved in the
likenesses of trees with little animals running up and down the trunks.

Rooms.Name: The Cozy Room
Rooms.Description:
You have entered a large, cozy living room. There is a fireplace with
a fire burning, and a few comfortable chairs around a little table.
There is a door to the west, and also an exit to the east.

Exits.Description: You see a large bedroom.
The door is large, and made out of oak.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The fire is built out of logs, and seems to be able to burn for 
quite a while longer.
The table is made of mahogany, and elegant in a cozy way(!)
The chairs are arranged around the fireplace.

Rooms.Name: The King's Bedroom
Rooms.Description:
This is a large room, with a wonderful view. To one side of the room,
stands a large four-poster bed. All around the room there are massive
bookshelves, filled with all kinds of books. The titles include works
such as: 'A Treatise on the History of Midgaard and surrounding areas',
'Magic - A Beginner's Introduction' and many others. There is an exit to
the west.

Exits.Description: There is a large and cozy room to the west.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Most of the books seem worn, as if thoroughly studied. The King
evidently is interested in keeping himself educated.

Seems nice enough to sleep in, though you would never dare to, since
it is a Royal Bed!
A dry tome, filled with boring knowledge.

Beginner? This book goes beyond most of what YOU know about magic
anyway. But then, there are levels of magical knowledge, it seems.

Rooms.Name: Up in the Tower
Rooms.Description:
After a long climb, you finally reach the top of the tower. This room
is small, and the only light source is a flickering candle, on a
cluttered table, in the middle of the room. The only obvious exit is
back down the stairs.

Exits.Description: The stairs go down the tower.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: On the table are various objects, all very strange-looking.
Small, uninteresting... A candle that is as normal as can be.

Rooms.Name: The Top of the Tower
Rooms.Description:
You have arrived at the top of the tower. This tower is pretty
uninteresting, and seems made purely for reasons of defense and
guarding. The windows are slits for bowmen, very narrow on the outward
side and broad inwards to allow a wide shooting angle. The only evident
exit is down the stairs again.

Exits.Description: The stairs go down to the second floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: As you look out the windows, you are granted a view of the country..

Rooms.Name: The Top of the Tower
Rooms.Description:
This is the highest of all the towers, and is obviously used for
lookout purposes. The view is splendid in all four directions. All
around you, the rich countryside spreads out to the horizon. To the
north and east you see a vast mountain range, and far to the west a
beautiful lake. A bit closer, the town of Midgaard lies at the end of
the King's Road. The only exit you can see is down again.

Exits.Description:
To the north, the tall White Mountains have their highest peaks. The
mountain tops disappear in the white clouds, far above the plains. The
sight of those high, far mountains fills you with a desire to scale
them, to see the world from that vantage.

In the east you see an arm of the dominating mountain range on this
continent, the White Mountains. Though not as high as those in the
north, the sight of those mountains fills you with awe.
To the south, rolling hills stretch away, as far as you can see.

As you look west, you see a river flowing through all of Midgaard and
continuing beyond it towards a great lake. Still further away, you can
glimpse something silvery that has to be the Sea.
You see the stairs going back down to the second floor.

Rooms.Name: Bottom of the Stairs
Rooms.Description:
At the bottom of a steep stone flight of stairs, you look around at the
well lit, but bare area.  There are two large hard chairs and a small
table.  On a small shelf built into the wall, you can see something
metallic, but the shelf is deep and shadowed.  There is a very heavy
door leading north.  It has a large sturdy knob and a keyhole the size
of a large walnut.

#GA few words have been carved on the lintel of the door north.#N

Exits.Description: A massive, heavy iron-bound door leads northward.
You see the stairs heading up to the main floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: #wAbandon Hope, All Ye Who Enter Here#N

Rooms.Name: Abandon Hope, All Ye Who Enter Here
Rooms.Description:
A small corridor leads to many cells, including one that appears to
hold many prisoners.  There is a distinctly evil feel to this room.  You
can feel the hair rising on the back of your neck.  The room is dimly
lit by two flickering torches resting in wall fixtures at about shoulder
height for a giant.  The stone floor is uneven beneath your feet, and
quite dirty.  You sense that the castles Cleaning Women do not make it
down this far.  There are doors leading in all directions, including a
heavy iron grate beneath your feet.  Each cell door has been labeled.

Exits.Description: Cell #1.  Heavy iron bars form the door to this cell.
Cell #2. A door of steel bars leads to another cell area.
A massive, heavy iron-bound door leads to a well-lit area.
Cell #3. A door of mithril and steel leads west.
A gagging smell rises from the oubliette.

Rooms.Name: A Large Cell
Rooms.Description:
This cell stretches as far as you can see, which actually isn't very
far considering the lighting.  A dim shroud of hopelessness envelops the
cell, a general cell for all of King Welmar's male prisoners.  Food is
delivered to the cell via the space beneath the door, and the water is a
simple trough, foul with dirt.  You fear venturing forward into this
nightmarish place, and should probably go south to the dismal entrance
room south.

Exits.Description: The gloom thickens north, east and west of where you quiver.
The gloom thickens north, east and west of where you shiver and shake.
Flickering torchlight beckons you away from the gloom.
The gloom thickens north, east and west of where you stand quivering.

Rooms.Name: Behind the Steel Bars
Rooms.Description:
As the cell is just barely lit by light reflected from the torches in
the room west of here, it is hard to make out any features of the room
itself or its inhabitants.  The floor feels hard beneath your feet,
undoubtedly the same stone as in the access room.  The walls are rough,
dirty, and slightly damp.  The stench is overwhelming.

Exits.Description: Steel bars form the door which leads out of the cell.

Rooms.Name: Cell Block #3
Rooms.Description:
The torch light from the entryway filters through the mithril and
steel bars forming part of the eastern wall of this cell.  Although by
no means well-lit, the openness of that wall allows you to see the straw
sleeping pallet in one corner, and the few hard crumbs remaining from a
recent meal.  The floor is bare, hard, and dirty as are the walls.
Being locked in here for a day would drive the sanest person mad.

Exits.Description: The small entry area lies east of here.

Rooms.Name: The Oubliette
Rooms.Description:
A heavy steel grate drops automatically into place overhead, blocking
even sound from above. This pit is one of several oubliettes in this
dungeon.  It is well-named.  Prisoners are placed (dropped?) in here and
then forgotten.  It is a slow death, as there is no escape possible.  As
you look around, you see the source of the horrifying odor rising from
this hole in the prison floor.
 
#GThe putrid remains of a prisoner lie here, rotting.#N

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Small bits of decaying flesh still hang on the bones, but not enough
to tell you who this once was.  The stench is overpowering.

Rooms.Name: Thickening gloom
Rooms.Description:
All around you you hear soft rustling noises of vermin, nesting in
the straw.  Occasionally a quiet moan reminds you that, incredibly,
there are prisoners still alive here.  The light is so dim that all
directions look the same to you.

Exits.Description: The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
A large door connects you to a torchlit room.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.

Rooms.Name: Thickening gloom
Rooms.Description:
All around you you hear soft rustling noises of vermin, nesting in
the straw.  Occasionally a quiet moan reminds you that, incredibly,
there are prisoners still alive here.  The light is so dim that all
directions look the same to you.

Exits.Description: The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.

Rooms.Name: Thickening gloom
Rooms.Description:
All around you you hear soft rustling noises of vermin, nesting in
the straw.  Occasionally a quiet moan reminds you that, incredibly,
there are prisoners still alive here.  The light is so dim that all
directions look the same to you.

Exits.Description: The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.
The gloom of endless suffering amidst endless evil beckons to you.

Rooms.Description:
All around you you hear soft rustling noises of vermin, nesting in
the straw.  Occasionally a quiet moan reminds you that, incredibly,
there are prisoners still alive here.  The light is so dim that all
directions look the same to you.

Rooms.Name: On the Outskirts of Midgaard
Rooms.Description:
The capital city of Midgaard generates a lot of traffic, and the
mayor and his councillors have chosen to encourage growth by improving
the many roads and waterways leading into the city.  The road is broad
and well-paved here.  It is rumored that Roman engineers were brought in
to design and supervise the building of this road.

Exits.Description:
The broad paved road leads east over hill and stream as far as you can
see.
To the west, the sounds and movement of city life increase dramatically.

Rooms.Name: Road Through Heavy Forest
Rooms.Description:
Trees thickly line the road to both north and south.  The forest
seems impenetrable here, and you wonder at the marvels of the Roman
engineers.  The well paved, Roman laid road continues east and west.

Exits.Description: The wide road continues east towards the kingdom of Welmar.
Midgaard, with all the delights of a capital city, lies to the west.

Rooms.Name: Road through Heavy Forest
Rooms.Description:
The well-paved road runs east and west, often thick with traffic.
Oxcarts bearing precious metals from the mountain mines, finely-made
dwarven armor, magic and herbs of elven origin - all travel this road at
some time, headed for the city of Midgaard.  With the many tradesmen
come artists and farmers and many who would train in the big city to
become master warriors and mages, clerics and healers and, yes, thieves
as well.

Exits.Description: The road appears to fork at some distance in the east.
A broad, well-paved, well-kept road makes its way towards Midgaard.

Rooms.Name: A Fork in the Road
Rooms.Description:
The Roman roadwork comes to an end at what is, nevertheless, a
magnificent intersection.  The southern fork follows the river for a
distance, heading for the magnificence of the kingdom of the good king
Welmar.  The other, more sinister fork, heads north into the great
purple mountains where, it is rumored, trolls lie in wait to munch
foolhardy adventurers.

Exits.Description: The road continues, rocky and rough, headed towards the foothills.

The road continues, wide and smooth, clearly well kept even though it is
no longer paved.

The beautifully paved, Roman-made road heads towards the splendors
of Midgaard.

Rooms.Name: A Well-Travelled Road
Rooms.Description:
The fine courtiers and nobles of the court of King Welmar travel this
road when they have business in the capital city of Midgaard.  The road
has been maintained at great cost to the wealthy king.  The forest on
both sides of the road is heavy.

Exits.Description: The road forks ahead, where Roman paving begins.
The forest begins to thin out ahead.

Rooms.Name: Thick Forest
Rooms.Description:
The thick forest continues to line both sides of the road, and to the
south you can hear the steady WHACK! Whack! of the lumberjack's axe.
The frenzied rate of building in this kingdom has increased the demand
for lumber.  There have been rumors that the trees scream in protest,
and darker rumors of hideous deaths of those found in the forest at
night.

Exits.Description:
The broad, hard packed road stretches very straightly north through
thick forest.
The thick forest crowds the road south.

Rooms.Name: Thick Forest
Rooms.Description:
Thick forest, old growth trees, crowd the wide road.  The road itself
winds slowly from north to east here, rolling around a gentle hill in
the deep forest.  An occasional WHACK! WHACK! of an axe is followed by
an eerie inhuman scream. There seems to be something strange about the
bushes to the west.

Exits.Description: The broad, well-packed dirt road heads north through thick forest.

The broad road winds east through gently rolling hills and thickly
encroaching forest.
You notice a narrow trail concealed in the undergrowth.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: There seems to be an opening of some sort behind the underbrush.

Rooms.Name: Thick Forest
Rooms.Description:
Closely spaced trees thin slightly to the east, creating a small
clearing.  The trees are tall and ancient, with branches which canopy
the roadway far over your head.  The result is a chill even in strong
sunlight, and an odd dappling pattern on the packed earthen road.

Exits.Description: It looks like there may be a small clearing just east of here.
The broad, tree-covered road continues westward.

Rooms.Name: A Clearing
Rooms.Description:
The trees have been thinned out here, clearly by man rather than fire
or disease.  There is a grassy area with many low stumps where you may
sit and rest, and a little trickle of a path runs north from the
clearing into the trees.

Exits.Description:
A thin, faint path leads into the trees.  It could simply be an animal
trail, or a path made by one of the elves native to this area.
The broad road continues east towards the great Kingdom of Welmar.
The broad road continues west towards the great city of Midgaard.

Rooms.Name: Through Thick Forest
Rooms.Description:
Pushing your way through lush green foliage, turning sideways to
slide through narrow gaps in trees, the reality of a path becomes
questionable.  Perhaps it is your imagine that sees a pattern in the
slight spacings between plants that leads you north from here.

Exits.Description:
Thick foliage (leaves of three, let it be ... better count them) must be
pushed aside if you wish to continue north.

If you are very careful and very skinny you can move through gaps in
trees and bushes and head south.

Rooms.Name: Brigands!
Rooms.Description:
A small camp here close to the castle shows the shabby flag of the
anti-monarchists, the revolutionaries of Welmar's kingdom.  In truth,
these revolutionaries support themselves by preying on hapless
travellers along the Welmar-Midgard highway.  A small tent sits at the
west end of the clearing.

Exits.Description:
The bushes and trees surrounding this camp seem slightly less thick to
the south.

A small tent made of elk and other animal hides sits at the west end of
this clearing.

Rooms.Name: Inside the Tent
Rooms.Description:
Strategy and planning sessions are held here in the tent of the
revolutionary leader Neb N'var.  Fiery speeches and sly plots are both
conceived in this tent, as is the next generation of revolutionaries.
The revolution has been a long time coming.

Exits.Description: The tent flap opens east.

Rooms.Name: The Well-Trod Road
Rooms.Description:
To the west lies a small clearing, perhaps a rest stop of sorts where
the weary traveller might regain his strength.  Or perhaps it is a trap
laid by one of the many groups of thieves you have heard roam this
forest despite King Welmar's best efforts.  This road continues both
east and west.

Exits.Description: The road east leads smoothly through thick forest.
The road west leads to a small clearing.  Picnic spot or trap?

Rooms.Name: Near a Bridge
Rooms.Description:
The sound of moving water drifts at you from the east, and in the
daytime you might be able to spot a castle from this spot.  You are
standing on a very wide, hardened dirt road leading west into deepest
forest and east to some body of water.

Exits.Description:
In the distance, for as far as you can see, lies thick forest, forest
which is apparently in a very bad mood.

Rooms.Name: Paving Stones
Rooms.Description:
The road at this point becomes paved with large flat white river
stones.  In the near distance to the east stands a magnificent old stone
bridge.  To the west, the thick forest continues.

Rooms.Name: Past the Fork
Rooms.Description:
The road deteriorates rapidly here deteriorating into a heavily
rutted cart track, much in used by both farmers and miners bringing
their wares to the city.  To the north, a new stronghold is being
built in a forest clearing.  South, the road becomes beautifully
paved.  This is the farmland of Welmar's mighty kingdom, perhaps.

Exits.Description: A stronghold is being constructed to the north.

Rooms.Name: The Glorious Bridge
Rooms.Description:
A very elaborate bridge stretches across the Midgaard River, which is
quite broad at this point.  At this end, the Midgaardian end, the bridge
is guarded by two enormous cast iron knights astride two even more
enormous cast iron horses.  The horses' teeth are bared and the knights
fists' are raised high in the air, clenching their swords.

Exits.Description:
An apparently strong bridge supported by stone arches spans the broad
expanse of the Midgaard River.

You can spot the western gates out of the City of Midgaard from this
point.
You can climb down to the Midgaard River.

Rooms.Name: Like a Bridge over Midgaard Waters
Rooms.Description:
A wide concrete bridge spans the troubled waters of the Midgaard
River.  Of Roman design and construction, you can tell that this is a
bridge which will be still standing here long after your many lives are
but a myth told over midnight glasses of ale at the local pub.

Exits.Description:
The wide and very sturdy bridge finishes its very long trip over the
River Midgaard just east of here.

Two huge knights mounted on fearsome horses challenge your right to
enter Midgaard.

Rooms.Name: Like a Bridge over Midgaard Waters
Rooms.Description:
Cast iron animals and odd misshapen figures appear to flee the brave
knights adorning the western (Midgaardian) end of this bridge.
Fantastical figures of fierce gryphons, drooling trolls, goblins and
orcs appear driven out of the city.  Perhaps this is meant as a warning.

Exits.Description:
A well made road clearly of Roman design proceeds in a grand manner
towards the rising sun.
A broad stone bridge spans the turbulent Midgaard River.

Rooms.Name: A Narrow Trail
Rooms.Description:
A narrow trail leads east and west from here, although some effort 
has been made to disguise the trail. The heavy paving slabs have been 
carefully concealed beneath a thick layer of earth and grass, with the 
stones only showing through in a few places.

Exits.Description: You see a wide road leading east.
The trail opens into a grassy meadow.

Mobs.Name: king welmar
Mobs.LongDescription: The wise King Welmar sits here in his throne.
Mobs.Description:
In his later middle-age, with his beard starting to grey, King Welmar is
still very powerfully built, and wouldn't take kindly to an attack.
Despite that, you know he is well-loved throughout the land, and has a
reputation as a wise and just ruler.

Mobs.Name: ghost horrible
Mobs.LongDescription: You hear a frightening wail, and see a horrible Ghost approaching.
Mobs.Description: The Ghost is almost translucent, and looks really SCARY!

Mobs.Name: jim guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Jim the Royal guard is here on duty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Jim wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and moves like an
experienced fighter.

Mobs.Name: brian guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Brian the Royal guard is here, training with the Master.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Brian wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and moves like an
experienced fighter.

Mobs.Name: mick guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Mick the Royal guard is here, training with the Master.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Mick wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and moves like an
experienced fighter.

Mobs.Name: matt guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Matt the Royal guard is here on duty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Matt wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and moves like an
experienced fighter.

Mobs.Name: jochem guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Jochem the Royal guard sits here, off duty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Jochem wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and moves like a fighter
who has seen more than one battle, and longs to see the next!

Mobs.Name: anne guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Anne the Royal guard is here on duty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Anne wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. She seems very well trained, and moves like a fighter
who has seen more than one battle, and longs to see the next!

Mobs.Name: andrew guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Andrew the Royal guard is here on duty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Andrew wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and moves like a fighter
who has seen more than one battle, and longs to see the next!

Mobs.Name: bertram bert guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Bertram the Royal guard is here on duty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Bertram wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and carries his scars
with pride. This guy seems tough...

Mobs.Name: jeanette guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Jeanette the Royal guard is here on duty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Jeanette wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. She seems very well trained, and carries her scars
with pride. This girl could be nasty if she wanted to...

Mobs.Name: peter captain guard royal
Mobs.ShortDescription: Peter, the Captain of the Royal guard
Mobs.LongDescription: Peter, the Captain of the Royal guard, walks around inspecting.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Peter wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. Even though all the other guards seem well trained,
you realise none of them would stand a chance against this man in a
fight. He stands at least two metres tall, but still moves with an
almost feline grace. He actually radiates strength and confidence,
and you have to fight a sudden urge to come to attention as you see
him.

Mobs.Name: master trainingmaster
Mobs.LongDescription: The Training Master is here, supervising.
Mobs.Description:
Aged, but experienced, the Training Master is skilled in the use
of virtually every weapon type invented by Man.

Mobs.Name: herald royal
Mobs.LongDescription: The Royal Herald is standing here.
Mobs.Description:
This is a young, powerfully built man, whose primary function
is to make Royal Announcements.

Mobs.Name: ergan murderer
Mobs.LongDescription: Slumped in a corner you see Ergan, aka the Murderer of Townsbridge.
Mobs.Description:
You remember a time almost a decade ago, when the news of the day
was how this man had slaughtered the entire population of the little
village of Townsbridge. He was imprisoned, and here he is: a shadow
of the undoubtedly great warrior he once was, but still to be reckoned
with.

Mobs.Name: butler james
Mobs.LongDescription: James the Butler is standing here, looking pompous.
Mobs.Description:
The typical perfect butler: upper middle age, a bit bald and with 
an impressive belly.

Mobs.Name: woman cleaning
Mobs.LongDescription: There is a cleaning woman here, trying not be noticed.
Mobs.Description: Although she has a menial job, she seems to like it.

Mobs.Name: astrologer
Mobs.LongDescription: The Astrologer is sitting here, studying a book.
Mobs.Description:
He is old and white-haired, with a long beard. As you see him, you
can almost believe the rumours about stars deciding Fate, and
that astrology is capable of seeing the future.

Mobs.Name: tim guard lifeguard
Mobs.LongDescription: Tim, the King's Lifeguard, is standing here.
Mobs.Description:
This guy looks just like his twin, Tom. There seems to be no
doubt that he is completely prepared to give his life
for the King, if necessary.

Mobs.Name: tom guard lifeguard
Mobs.LongDescription: Tom, the King's Lifeguard, is standing here.
Mobs.Description:
This guy looks just like his twin, Tim. There seems to be no
doubt that he is completely prepared to give his life
for the King, if necessary.

Mobs.Name: chef cook
Mobs.LongDescription: The Chef is here, shouting orders to the other cooks.
Mobs.Description:
It seems he has been tasting his own food a bit too enthusiastically.
He is, in other words, a bit fat.

Mobs.Name: cook
Mobs.LongDescription: A junior cook makes himself busy stirring a pot.
Mobs.Description: A junior cook, eager to do the Chef's bidding.

Mobs.Name: david guard
Mobs.LongDescription: David, a big, mean-looking man, stands here, guarding the door.
Mobs.Description:
He really is big, and you get the feeling he wouldn't take kindly
to an attempt to get past him.

Mobs.Name: dick guard
Mobs.LongDescription: Dick, a big, mean-looking man, stands here, guarding the door.
Mobs.Description:
He really is big, and you get the feeling he wouldn't take kindly
to an attempt to get past him.

Mobs.Name: jerry guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Jerry the Royal guard is here off duty, playing dice.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Jerry wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and moves like an
experienced fighter.

Mobs.Name: michael guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Michael the Royal guard is here off duty, playing dice.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Michael wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and moves like an
experienced fighter.

Mobs.Name: hans guard royal
Mobs.LongDescription: Hans the Royal guard is here on duty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Hans wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and moves like a fighter
who has seen more than one battle, and longs to see the next!

Mobs.Name: boris guard royal m15029
Mobs.LongDescription: Boris the Royal guard is here on duty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Guard, Boris wears the chain mail required of
them as uniform. He seems very well trained, and carries his scars
with pride. This guy seems tough...

Mobs.Name: Morianne queen m15030
Mobs.LongDescription: Lovely Queen Morianne moves gracefully about the room.
Mobs.Description:
The daughter of the Grand Mistress, the frightening witch who lives in a
Tower of Sorcery, Morianne has managed to avoid her mother's evil
habits.  She is as pure and lovely as her husband is good and wise.

Mobs.Name: Petunia attendant lady lady-in-waiting m15031
Mobs.LongDescription: Petunia the Queen's lady-in-waiting is helping her majesty.
Mobs.Description:
As all members of the Queen's personal staff, Petunia is the quite
lovely daughter of one of the local nobles.  The Queen hopes to marry
her off soon, as her personality is quite grating.

Mobs.Name: Pansy lady lady-in-waiting m15032
Mobs.LongDescription: Pansy looks at you from eyes the color of crushed violets.
Mobs.Description:
Pansy has a way of getting what she wants from the queen or, indeed, any
member of the court.  She is extremely beautiful, and appears quite
vulnerable.  In fact, of course, she is extremely strong.

Mobs.Name: Tulip lady m15033
Mobs.LongDescription: Tulip struts arrogantly about the room, stopping only at mirrors.
Mobs.Description:
With long blond hair braided in the latest fashion to hit the court,
wearing only the latest and most costly of gowns, Tulip feels she is not
arrogant, just very aware of her place as the most eligible of the
ladies in waiting.

Mobs.Name: m15034 sergei guard dungeon
Mobs.LongDescription:
Sergei the dungeon guard stands here, seemingly watching everything
at once.
Mobs.Description:
Although he never seems to move and inch he appears to be seeing
everything around him simultaneously.  For that matter, you can't
imagine anything could possibly move Sergei; he is easily one of
the largest men you have ever seen.  His armor is worn and dirty,
casting him as a huge black figure.  It's no wonder no one ever
escapes from this dungeon.

Mobs.Name: m15035 nikolas guard dungeon
Mobs.LongDescription:
Nikolas the dungeon guard stands here, seemingly watching everything
at once.
Mobs.Description:
Although he never seems to move and inch he appears to be seeing
everything around him simultaneously.  For that matter, you can't
imagine anything could possibly move Nikolas; he is easily one of
the largest men you have ever seen.  His armor is worn and dirty,
casting him as a huge black figure.  It's no wonder no one ever
escapes from this dungeon.

Mobs.Name: m15036 prisoner heretic reb'malim rebmalim
Mobs.LongDescription: The moronic heretic named Reb'Malim stands here, stupidly.
Mobs.Description:
This prisoner is guilty of heresy against the Gods, by using unethical
alchemy to reproduce gold and magical items.  At first you fear his
cunning, but when you look into his eyes, you realize that there isn't
much there...

Mobs.Name: m15037 prisoner murderer jack
Mobs.LongDescription: Jack, the cowardly murderer is huddled in the corner.
Mobs.Description:
This prisoner is guilty of luring and murdering the young, innocent, and
inexperienced.  Have no mercy for this coward, for he deserves none.

Mobs.Name: m15038 prisoner burnt bread toast
Mobs.LongDescription: A heinous prisoner, known only as burnt bread stands here.
Mobs.Description:
One of the dungeons many captives stands before you, smelling faintly of
stale, cooked bread.  His crimes are otherworldly and unspeakable...
Things mortal man were not meant to understand, yet he is so irritating
you would not dream of questioning his imprisonment.

Mobs.Name: m15039 prisoner pedro alonso lopez
Mobs.ShortDescription: Pedro Alonso Lopez, "Monster of the Andes"
Mobs.LongDescription: Pedro Alonso Lopez stands here, planning future slayings.
Mobs.Description:
Estimated at killing over three hundred young girls, Lopez's childhood
is marked by his mother's prostitution, molesting his sister, and
finally his own sodomy by a pedophile.  He is truly a product of his
environment.

Mobs.Name: m15040 prisoner sadist king henry lee lucas
Mobs.LongDescription: Henry Lee Lucas stands here, day dreaming about animals and corpses.
Mobs.Description:
Lucas's nickname of "Sadist King" doesn't even begin to describe his
depravity.  Guilty of many, many murders, he also took pleasure in
matricide, necrophilia, and bestiality.  Forever linked with his partner
in crime, Ottis Toole.

Mobs.Name: m15041 prisoner ottis toole generalissimo pain
Mobs.LongDescription: Ottis Toole, the deeply psychotic retard, stands here.
Mobs.Description:
Ottis Toole complements his partner in crime, Henry Lee Lucas, perfectly.
He is a transvestite mass murderer with a taste for human flesh.  He
also claims to be a close associate of Jim Jones.
Mobs.ActionScript: %%10 drool;%10 twitch;%10 emote eyes you, hungrily.

Mobs.Name: m15042 prisoner doctor holmes dr
Mobs.LongDescription: Dr. Holmes stands here, contemplating your demise.
Mobs.Description:
Dr. Holmes started his career as a medical student by stealing corpses
from his University.  He used insurance fraud to raise enough money to
construct a castle filled with torturous devices, which he later had to
torch to destroy evidence of his murders.

Mobs.Name: higglebottom Mrs. housekeeper m15043
Mobs.LongDescription: Mrs. Higglebottom, King Welmar's housekeeper, bustles about tidying up.
Mobs.Description:
Mrs. Higglebottom is a short, round woman of indeterminate age.  Her
title is honorary, as there is nothing to indicate there was ever a Mr.
Higglebottom.  She seems to have been at the castle forever.  She makes
sure the cleaning ladies do their jobs properly and that the castle is
run in an orderly fashion.

Mobs.Name: m15044 advisor Parassus
Mobs.LongDescription: Parassus, the king's advisor, wears a strange insignia around his neck.
Mobs.Description:
A tall, gaunt human with long, dark hair, high cheekbones, and deep blue
eyes that never quite meet yours, Parassus has been the king's advisor
since Nilrem mysteriously disappeared.  King Welmar relies on him
absolutely, seemingly oblivious to the advisor's occasional (hiss) and
his fiery explosions of temper.

Mobs.Name: court mage m15045
Mobs.LongDescription: The mage dressed in forest green peers out from under bushy white brows.
Mobs.Description:
Thick snow white hair floats wildly about the tall, slender mage's head,
effectively hiding the gentle points of his ears.  As Chief Mage to His
Majesty, King Welmar, he is allowed, even expected to have his
eccentricities.  Nobody knows that his preference for green comes from
his secret alliance with his brethern in the Free the Elves foundation.

Mobs.Name: priest court highpriest m15046
Mobs.LongDescription:
Trained by the avatar at a small temple near Moria, the High 
Priest is feared.
Mobs.Description:
If ever there were a warrior priest, this man fulfills the description.
He is the second son of a Duke of the Realm of King Welmar.  He is quite
tall, well over six and a half feet (over 2m), and as broad of shoulder
as a minotaur.  His high forehead leads to long thick brown hair, tied
back with a leather thong.  The priest watches carefully over the
spiritual health of the castle inhabitants, and is likely to order a
flogging of a miscreant.

Mobs.Name: prisoner thief
Mobs.LongDescription: A captured thief is imprisoned here, wishing for death.
Mobs.Description:
Standing at about 5'8", this thief doesn't seem very dangerous at all.
Perhaps he was just stealing some food for his family.  Since he still
has one hand he probably was only caught once.

Mobs.Name: prisoner peeping tom
Mobs.LongDescription: A peeping Tom wanders around here, looking embarassed.
Mobs.Description:
Even minor crimes of perversion are punishable by life imprisonment in
Welmar's domain.  You better keep your eyes to yourself.

Mobs.Name: prisoner political
Mobs.LongDescription: A political prisoner runs around, frustrated by his capture.
Mobs.Description:
This young man's life came to an accelerated end after being foolish
enough to support one of Welmar's opponents.  Let this be a lesson to
all would-be fanatics, "Don't mess with the King."

Mobs.Name: man young travelling warrior
Mobs.LongDescription: A young man hurries towards Midgaard, determined to become a warrior.
Mobs.Description:
All his life he has dreamed of becoming a warrior, fighting dragons
and rescuing maidens in distress. Now he is off to Midgaard to make
his dreams come true!

Mobs.Name: dispatch runner
Mobs.LongDescription: A dispatch runner hurries along the road, to deliver important messages.
Mobs.Description:
The key to ruling a kingdom is communication. King Welmars dispatch 
runners travel all over the world delivering his missives.

Mobs.Name: child adventurous
Mobs.LongDescription: An adventurous young child is looking for excitement.
Mobs.Description:
This mischevious child has sneaked away to look for adventure. Who knows?
Perhaps she will find it?

Mobs.Name: soldier patrolling
Mobs.LongDescription: A soldier is patrolling this area.
Mobs.Description:
This confident looking soldier patrols the road between Midgaard and
King Welmars castle, protecting people from bandits.

Mobs.Name: mage wandering apprentice
Mobs.LongDescription: An apprentice mage is wandering along the road.
Mobs.Description:
The mage doesnt look very powerful. Her hat is not very pointy and her
robe has only got a few straggly looking stars on it. She hopes to find
a powerful master on her travels and become his apprentice.

Mobs.Name: fairy cheeky druid
Mobs.LongDescription: A cheeky fairy pokes her tongue out at you!
Mobs.Description: How rude! But you guess she's just teasing.

Mobs.Name: elf elven ranger
Mobs.LongDescription: A willowy elven ranger looks about, ready to disappear into the forest.
Mobs.Description:
In his dark green clothing, and carrying his bow, he looks ready to 
vanish into the forest at a moments notice.

Mobs.Name: priest
Mobs.LongDescription: An old priest limps slowly towards Midgaard
Mobs.Description:
Dressed in ragged priests robes, and clutching a gnarled walking staff
the priest slowly makes his way home towards Midgaard.

Mobs.Name: guard guardsman welmars royal
Mobs.LongDescription: An armored guardsman marches purposefully towards Welmars Castle.
Mobs.Description:
He marches with a self importantly towards King Welmars castle, watching
the forest on all sides for brigands and thieves.

Mobs.Name: brigand robber revolutionary
Mobs.LongDescription: A rough looking young brigand is startled by your arrival.
Mobs.Description:
Surely too young to be away from home, this idealistic young revolutionary 
has run away to join Iram Ashmar's anti-monarchy revolution. It is not all 
living in the forest and eating bark you know, sometimes they have to run 
away from soldiers too.

Mobs.Name: neb nvar n'var revolutionary leader brigand
Mobs.LongDescription: Neb N'var, the leader of the revolution, tries to bring you to his cause.
Mobs.Description:
A very charismatic man, with a sharp moustache and quick smile. He 
immediately tries to convince you to join his band with a rakish smile and 
the promise of glory and justice for the common people.

Objects.Name: sceptre royal golden
Objects.Description: A golden Royal sceptre lies on the ground.

Objects.Name: crown golden
Objects.Description: A magnificently jewelled golden crown has been left here.

Objects.Name: apple golden
Objects.Description: There is a golden apple here.

Objects.Name: telescope scope
Objects.Description: There is a large telescope here, pointing at the sky.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: A small sign says: Made in Tynstri.

Objects.Name: sword training
Objects.Description: A training sword with blunt edges leans against a wall.

Objects.Name: key huge
Objects.Description: There is a huge, heavy-looking key on the floor here.

Objects.Name: key butlers butler
Objects.Description: The Butler's key is here.

Objects.Name: key small
Objects.Description: A small key lies here.

Objects.Name: chest wooden
Objects.Description: A large wooden chest stands here in a corner.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It is equipped with a small lock, that any self-respecting thief
should be able to pick.

Objects.Name: vial large potion brown
Objects.Description: A large vial has been left here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It is filled with a disgusting brown liquid.

Objects.Name: banner royal
Objects.Description: The royal banner has been firmly planted in the ground here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It is large and very heavy. On top of it flutters King Welmar's flag
proudly.
On the flag is the symbol of King Welmar's house, the rampant stag.

Objects.Name: key
Objects.Description: A key lies on the floor.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It has a finely carved letter 'W' inscribed on it.

Objects.Name: mail chain hauberk
Objects.Description: A chain mail hauberk lies on the floor

Objects.Name: sword large broadsword
Objects.Description: A large broadsword has been dropped.

Objects.Name: lobster
Objects.Description: A delicious-looking lobster tempts your appetite.

Objects.Name: caviar
Objects.Description:
There is some delicious-looking Russian caviar which makes your mouth
water.

Objects.Name: key
Objects.Description: The end of this key is as large as a walnut.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It is particularly uninspiring.

Objects.Name: key
Objects.Description: The iron key is marked with the number "1".

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It is particularly uninspiring.

Objects.Name: key
Objects.Description: The large steel key is marked with the number "2".

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It is marked with the number 2.

Objects.Name: key
Objects.Description: This key is made of mithril.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It is marked with a large number 3.

Objects.Name: key
Objects.Description: This key looks forgotten.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: An iron key marked with the letter "O".

Objects.Name: shelf shelves
Objects.Description: #G

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It looks like there might be something way at the back of the shelf.
You know it isn't dust!

Objects.Name: staff gnarled walking
Objects.Description: A gnarled walking staff has been left here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It looks like it would make an excellent support for an unsteady walker. On
the other hand, it looks like it could be used to give any troublemakers a
jolly good drubbing.

Objects.Name: ring neb nvar revolution revolutionary
Objects.Description: A revolutionary's ring defies you to pick it up.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
This is the signet ring of revolution leader Neb N'var. Only leaders of
the revolution wear rings like this. Death to the Monarchy!

Objects.Name: sword plain
Objects.Description: A plain undorned sword looks servicable enough.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It looks like that kind of sword that a regular soldier would use, not
especially well made, but perfectly servicable, and by the shimmering
blade you guess that some magic user has placed some rudimentary 
enchantment upon it.

Objects.Name: longbow rangers elven
Objects.Description: An elven ranger has left his longbow, he will not be far away!

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The reputation of elven rangers owes a great deal to the longbow. It
truely is a magnificent weapon.

Objects.Name: gold coins
Objects.Description: A lot of gold is here.

Objects.Name: dagger
Objects.Description: A dagger with a long thin blade is here.

Objects.Name: sword small
Objects.Description: A small sword lies here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The small sword seems to have an inscription of some sort inscription...
It says: "May this sword be a good companion."

Objects.Name: sword long
Objects.Description: A long sword has been left here.

Objects.Name: club wooden
Objects.Description: A simple looking wooden club is here.

Objects.Name: scroll identify
Objects.Description: A scroll has carelessly been left here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The scroll has a magic formula drawn upon it:
     ???
    ?   ?
       ?
      ?
      ?
      *

Objects.Name: scroll recall
Objects.Description: A scroll has carelessly been left here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The scroll has written a formulae of 'Word of Recall' upon it.
